principles: One canonical acceptance truth source; topology references verificationIntent declarations and verifier-derived basis only.
Fail closed on missing, partial, unsupported, stale, tampered or caller-authored authority.
Recompute against the current worktree at DEV-to-REVIEW and bind every consumed fact to signed hashes.
Preserve explicit observe, warn and enforce rollback while keeping Wave 3A and Wave 4 out of scope.
drivers: Prevent omissions from being discovered only after expensive reviewer rounds.
Reuse existing phaseBasis=pre_review, canonical evidence refs and freshness readers without parallel truth stores.
Maintain backward compatibility and deterministic process-fact contracts across CLI and lifecycle consumers.

options.name: A: Read-only recomputation only
cons: No durable signed receipt for reviewer/audit consumption
Harder to prove exact producer-verifier-lifecycle parity and replay/tamper behavior

options.name: B: Verifier-owned signed pre-review artifact plus read-only evaluator
pros: Lifecycle and CLI can share one canonical verifier
Supports precise stale/tamper/mutation diagnostics without caller authority
cons: Adds one lifecycle artifact and signing/freshness surface
Requires careful metadata classification and restoration tests

options.name: C: Extend acceptance-basis receipt to carry final verdict
cons: Conflates coverage discovery with executable evidence verdict
Risks weakening canonical ownership and complicates PLAN compatibility

chosen: B: Verifier-owned signed pre-review artifact plus read-only evaluator
rationale: Option B cleanly separates coverage-basis discovery from executable pre-review proof while giving the DEV-to-REVIEW gate a durable signed artifact whose inputs can be independently recomputed. It provides the auditability and mutation bite required by Wave 3 without duplicating topology or allowing callers to write authority.

preMortem.scenario: A stale pre-review receipt passes after implementation or evidence changes.
preMortem.trigger: Verifier checks signature but omits storyFilesHash, evidence digest, basis digest or current freshness recomputation.
preMortem.consequence: Reviewer rounds consume proof for a different worktree and omissions reach REVIEW.
preMortem.mitigation: Bind and recompute plan/pre-review basis, topology, scope, story/closure hashes, evidence set and freshness; mutation-test each field and replay.

preMortem.scenario: The new gate deadlocks all legacy or observe-mode Stories.
preMortem.trigger: DEV-to-REVIEW always requires a Wave 3 artifact regardless of configured mode or applicability contract.
preMortem.consequence: Unrelated Stories cannot enter REVIEW and operators bypass the gate.
preMortem.mitigation: Reuse existing observe/warn/enforce mode, keep observe non-blocking diagnostics, add legacy compatibility controls and rollback tests.

preMortem.scenario: Caller-controlled evidence or prose can manufacture PASS.
preMortem.trigger: Command accepts inventory, verdict, authority, transcript relation or mutation status from CLI arguments or notes.
preMortem.consequence: A self-authored false-green receipt satisfies the lifecycle gate.
preMortem.mitigation: Accept only storyId; derive all facts from store, git, signed artifacts and registered provenance; reject prompt labels and unverified notes.

preMortem.scenario: Omission test passes because topology and basis are mutated together.
preMortem.trigger: Test deletes the same path from both truth inputs before evaluation.
preMortem.consequence: The exact omission class that caused repeated REVIEW gaps remains invisible.
preMortem.mitigation: Hold current recomputed basis fixed, delete only the topology mapping, require AT_UNMAPPED_SCOPE_REF, then byte-restore and prove PASS.

preMortem.scenario: The implementation accidentally claims Wave 3A or Wave 4 rollout.
preMortem.trigger: Gate mode selection is inferred from risk keywords or prompts are changed to enforce globally.
preMortem.consequence: Existing Stories change behavior without approved applicability or measured thresholds.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep flat project mode only, explicitly assert no selective resolver/telemetry rollout assets, and mutation-test later-wave leakage.
